entries.title: 3D-Glasring, vom Scrollen gesteuert
items: Rebuild the homepage around a 3D glass ring driven by scroll

lumiere-gl.js: a WebGL torus in gold-tinted glass, built with three.js and bundled with esbuild down to what it actually uses (530 KB raw, 136 KB gzipped, instead of the full 2.1 MB). The environment it refracts is drawn on a canvas at runtime, so nothing is fetched.
its path is a keyframe table, not trigonometry, so a single scene can be adjusted without bending the whole curve
scenes now alternate left, right and centre and enter from the side they come from, instead of all being centred
the ring turns translucent where it crosses type, and fades out once the footer arrives, so nothing it passes behind becomes unreadable
light streaks at the cursor are longer and vary in temperature across the gold palette, from amber to champagne
lower-powered devices get the same staging more cheaply: polished metal instead of refracting glass, fewer motes, half the pixel ratio, and a smaller ring on portrait screens
no WebGL at all falls back to a CSS emblem; reduced motion holds the ring still and redraws it once per scroll
Document how the ring bundle is rebuilt

Follows the supplied footer anatomy: centred glow above the top border, bordered column grid with dividers, a large jump card with arrow per column plus a group of small links, and a centred copyright bar. Links point only at destinations that actually exist and reuse goToDestination(), so the existing lock badges appear automatically via updateGatedNavUI(). Stacks to one column on phones.

Feature card icons redrawn as the orb from the cards prompt: round body, dashed ring, offset outline and a soft glow that fades in behind the icon on hover (glow sits below the icon so it never obscures it).

Hero shader from the hero prompt, as an ambient backdrop behind the existing Berlin-Paris map rather than replacing it - that map is custom work and a generic library visual would be a downgrade. Deliberately defensive: pointer devices with WebGL2 only, off under reduced motion and on touch, masked out towards the bottom at 50% opacity so the headline stays readable, height capped to the hero (.hub-hero-bg spans the whole hub, so an uncapped canvas would shade the entire page), resolution capped at 1.5x, and the loop pauses when the hub is hidden or the tab is in the background. Added a lumiere:viewchange event for that pausing.

Replaced all optional chaining (?.) and nullish coalescing (??). Both need Safari 13.1+, and these are parse-time features: on an older iPad the whole script would fail to parse, not just the affected line. Now parses back to roughly iOS 11.
Fix tab indicator never animating, longer card texts, map image fallback

The login/register tab indicator never actually animated. It moved with translateX(calc(100% + .25rem)), and transform percentages resolve against the element's OWN width - which here is itself a percentage of the parent. Until that resolved, 100% was simply 0, so the pill sat on "Anmelden" for about half a second and then jumped across. getAnimations() returned an empty array: no transition was running at all, reproducibly across runs. Now driven by `left`, whose percentages resolve against the parent and are stable. Verified: a real 400ms CSSTransition on `left` now runs on each switch, in both directions.
Feature card descriptions rewritten from one short clause into a full sentence each, as requested. Checked at 1500/1280/834/390px: nothing is clipped and cards stay aligned within each row.

The hero map photo now hides itself if it fails to load instead of sprawling its alt text across the map. This is what showed up when index.html was opened on its own without the image files next to it; the SVG map underneath carries the card fine on its own. On the deployed site the image serves normally (verified: HTTP 200, valid 1408x768 JPEG).
Add empty states with actions, typed toasts and magnetic buttons

Empty states (interactive-empty-state): the "no sets" and "no vocab" states were an icon plus one line of text with no way forward. Now they follow the supplied anatomy - three tiles fanning apart on hover, a title, an explanation, and a button that performs the actual action (opens the new-set dialog / focuses the vocab field). A dead end with no next step was the weakest spot on the site.

Toasts: showToast() rendered plain text, so nothing distinguished success from failure but the border colour. Now each has an icon and a type (success / error / info). The old boolean second argument still works, so no call site needed changing.

Magnetic buttons (Magnetic): primary buttons, the footer cards and the empty-state actions drift toward the pointer within range and spring back. One global pointermove handler rather than a listener per button. Off on touch and under reduced motion.
